items.name: Veterans Crisis Line
items.description: 24/7 confidential support for Veterans, service members, Guard/Reserve, and their families. Dial 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat online. No VA enrollment required.

items.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
items.description: Free, confidential 24/7 VA hotline (877-424-3838) for Veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing housing. Counselors connect you to local VA homeless services.

items.name: Military OneSource
items.description: DoD-funded 24/7 information and referral hub for service members, families, and survivors—counseling, financial help, relocation, and crisis support.

items.name: Give an Hour
items.description: Nonprofit network that connects military members, Veterans, and families to free or low-cost mental health care and peer support.

items.name: The Headstrong Project
items.description: Confidential, no-cost mental health treatment for post-9/11 Veterans and families; focuses on trauma-informed care without VA bureaucracy.

items.name: VA Suicide Prevention
items.description: VA suicide-prevention overview with crisis contacts, local resource locator links, and how to reach suicide prevention coordinators.

items.name: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA.gov)
items.description: Primary portal for VA health care, disability claims, education benefits, home loans, life insurance, and burial benefits. Apply and manage benefits online.

items.name: milConnect
items.description: DoD portal to manage DEERS, view military records, print proof of coverage, and access transition documents including VMET.

items.name: TRICARE
items.description: Military health plan for active duty, retirees, Guard/Reserve, and eligible family members. Enrollment, plan comparison, and provider search.

items.name: Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS)
items.description: Official system that records eligibility for military benefits. Update addresses, dependents, and ID card information through milConnect or a RAPIDS site.

items.name: VA Mental Health
items.description: VA overview of mental health programs, how to get care, and links to crisis resources and specialty clinics.

items.name: DoD Transition Assistance Program (TAP)
items.description: Official DoD TAP portal for separating and retiring service members—mandatory briefs, career readiness standards, and DD Form 2648.

items.name: DoD SkillBridge
items.description: Allows eligible service members within 180 days of separation to train with civilian employers while still on active duty (with command approval).

items.name: My HealtheVet / VA Health & Benefits App
items.description: Start from VA.gov to refill prescriptions, message care teams, and manage appointments and benefits on web or mobile.

items.name: Disabled American Veterans (DAV)
items.description: VSO that files and appeals VA disability claims at no cost, plus transportation to VA medical appointments and employment programs.

items.name: Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW)
items.description: National VSO offering free VA claims assistance, advocacy, financial grants, and local post support for combat and overseas Veterans.

items.name: The American Legion
items.description: Largest U.S. veterans service organization; provides claims help, community programs, and advocacy on VA and DoD issues.

items.name: Paralyzed Veterans of America (PVA)
items.description: VSO focused on Veterans with spinal cord injury/disease, MS, and ALS—claims representation, advocacy, and specialized care support.

items.name: AMVETS
items.description: Veterans service organization providing free claims representation, employment services, and local posts open to nearly all honorably discharged Veterans.

items.name: Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA)
items.description: Post-9/11 Veterans advocacy organization focused on mental health, benefits access, and policy for GWOT-era service members.

items.name: National Veterans Legal Services Program (NVLSP)
items.description: Nonprofit law firm that trains VSOs and provides free legal help on VA benefits, discharge upgrades, and caregiver appeals.

items.name: VA Disability Compensation
items.description: Official VA page to file and manage disability compensation claims for service-connected conditions.

items.name: VA Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E)
items.description: Chapter 31 program for Veterans with service-connected disabilities—training, education, job placement, and independent living support.

items.name: VA Claims Appeals (Board of Veterans’ Appeals)
items.description: Official paths to request a Higher-Level Review, Supplemental Claim, or Board Appeal if you disagree with a VA benefits decision.

items.name: Make the Connection
items.description: VA site with Veteran stories and mental health resources covering PTSD, depression, substance use, and how to seek care.

items.name: National Center for PTSD
items.description: VA research and education center on PTSD—treatment options, apps (including PTSD Coach), and guidance for Veterans and families.

items.name: PTSD Coach
items.description: Free VA mobile app for managing PTSD symptoms with tools, education, and self-assessment. Available without VA enrollment.

items.name: Cohen Veterans Network
items.description: National network of mental health clinics offering accessible care for post-9/11 Veterans, service members, and families.

items.name: Wounded Warrior Project
items.description: Programs for post-9/11 wounded, ill, or injured Veterans—mental health, peer support, benefits counseling, and family services at no cost.

items.name: Hope For The Warriors
items.description: Supports post-9/11 service members, Veterans, and families with clinical care, peer programs, and transition resources.

items.name: PsychArmor
items.description: Free online courses that train clinicians, employers, and communities to work effectively with Veterans and military families.

items.name: Team Red, White & Blue (Team RWB)
items.description: Community fitness and belonging organization connecting Veterans through workouts, events, and local chapters nationwide.

items.name: VA Mental Health — Get Help
items.description: VA landing page for getting mental health help, including crisis options and how to start care through VA.

items.name: VA Homeless Programs
items.description: Overview of VA housing and homelessness services, including how to reach local Homeless Coordinators and national hotlines.

items.name: HUD-VASH
items.description: Joint HUD–VA program pairing Housing Choice Vouchers with VA case management for homeless Veterans and their families.

items.name: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
items.description: VA-funded community program that prevents homelessness and rapidly re-houses very low-income Veteran families.

items.name: National Coalition for Homeless Veterans (NCHV)
items.description: National advocacy and capacity-building group focused on ending Veteran homelessness; connects Veterans to local providers.

items.name: VA Home Loans
items.description: VA-backed home loan benefits for eligible Veterans, service members, and surviving spouses—purchase, refinance, and Certificate of Eligibility.

items.name: Operation Homefront — Housing
items.description: Nonprofit housing programs for military and Veteran families, including transitional and permanent housing support.

items.name: Volunteers of America — Veteran Services
items.description: National nonprofit providing housing, case management, employment, and behavioral health services for Veterans and families.

items.name: HUD Homeless Veterans / HUD-VASH Overview
items.description: HUD’s public-facing overview of HUD-VASH vouchers and how public housing authorities partner with VA for Veteran housing.

items.name: Hire Heroes USA
items.description: Free one-on-one career coaching, resume help, and interview prep for transitioning service members, Veterans, and military spouses.

items.name: Hiring Our Heroes
items.description: U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation program with hiring events, SkillBridge fellowships, and career services for the military community.

items.name: USAJOBS — Veterans
items.description: Federal job portal with Veterans’ Preference guidance, special hiring authorities, and how to apply for government careers.

items.name: Department of Labor VETS
items.description: DoL Veterans’ Employment and Training Service—employment rights (USERRA), Jobs for Veterans State Grants, and transition employment navigators.

items.name: Helmets to Hardhats
items.description: Connects Veterans to union construction apprenticeships and skilled-trades careers with earn-while-you-learn pathways.

items.name: American Corporate Partners (ACP)
items.description: Free year-long mentoring program pairing Veterans and military spouses with corporate professionals for career guidance.

items.name: Onward to Opportunity (O2O) — IVMF
items.description: Syracuse University IVMF program offering free career training, industry certifications, and job placement support for Veterans and spouses.

items.name: VetJobs
items.description: Employment nonprofit helping Veterans and military spouses find civilian jobs through recruiting support and employer partnerships.

items.name: FourBlock
items.description: Free career-readiness courses and coaching that help Veterans and military spouses translate military experience for civilian employers.

items.name: Combined Arms
items.description: Veteran-built referral network linking service members, Veterans, and families to 300+ vetted resources across all 50 states.

items.name: DoL Employment Navigator and Partnership Program
items.description: Personalized employment navigation for transitioning service members, with referrals to partner career programs.

items.name: VA Education & Training (GI Bill)
items.description: Official VA hub for Post-9/11 GI Bill, Montgomery GI Bill, and other education benefits—eligibility, applications, and payment info.

items.name: GI Bill Comparison Tool / Education Benefits Overview
items.description: Plain-language VA guide to GI Bill benefit types, housing allowance, and what each chapter covers.

items.name: Student Veterans of America (SVA)
items.description: National network of 1,600+ campus chapters supporting student Veterans with leadership programs, advocacy, and peer community.

items.name: VA Yellow Ribbon Program
items.description: Partnership between VA and schools that can cover tuition beyond the Post-9/11 GI Bill annual cap at participating institutions.

items.name: Veterans Education Success (VES)
items.description: Nonprofit that helps student Veterans with GI Bill problems, school complaints, career counseling, and free legal advice related to education benefits.

items.name: VA VET TEC 2.0 / High-Tech Training
items.description: VA education portal covering high-tech training pathways and related education benefits for eligible Veterans and service members.

items.name: GI Bill Hotline
items.description: Call 888-442-4551 (888-GIBILL-1) for official help with GI Bill applications, payments, and school certification questions.

items.name: VA Caregiver Support Program
items.description: VA program for family caregivers—training, peer support, and applications for the Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC).

items.name: Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers
items.description: VA caregiver benefit that may include a monthly stipend, health coverage (CHAMPVA), respite, and training for eligible Veterans’ caregivers.

items.name: Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS)
items.description: 24/7 grief support for survivors of fallen military members—peer mentoring, counseling referrals, and survivor community.

items.name: Fisher House Foundation
items.description: Provides free lodging near military and VA medical centers for families of wounded, ill, or injured service members and Veterans.

items.name: Blue Star Families
items.description: Nonprofit connecting military and Veteran families through local chapters, research, spouse career support, and community programs.

items.name: National Military Family Association (NMFA)
items.description: Advocacy and programs for military families, including spouse scholarships and policy work on quality-of-life issues.

items.name: Operation Homefront
items.description: Financial assistance, housing support, and family programs for active-duty and Veteran families facing hardship.

items.name: Soldiers’ Angels
items.description: Volunteer-driven aid including care packages, food assistance, and support for deployed troops, Veterans, and military families.

items.name: Semper Fi & America’s Fund
items.description: Lifetime case management and financial support for critically wounded, ill, or injured service members, Veterans, and families across all branches.

items.name: Elizabeth Dole Foundation — Hidden Heroes
items.description: National community and resource hub for military and Veteran caregivers, including education, peer connection, and advocacy.

items.name: Code of Support Foundation
items.description: Connects Veterans, service members, caregivers, and families to vetted resources through case coordination and the PATRIOTlink network.

items.name: VA Center for Women Veterans
items.description: VA office that advocates for women Veterans’ access to benefits, health care, and recognition across the VA system.

items.name: Women Veterans Call Center
items.description: Free, confidential VA line (1-855-829-6636) for women Veterans seeking help with health care, benefits, and local resources.

items.name: Service Women’s Action Network (SWAN)
items.description: Independent advocacy and case-management organization focused on servicewomen and women Veterans, including MST-related support.

items.name: VA Women Veterans Health Care
items.description: VA women’s health portal covering primary care, reproductive health, MST care, and how to find a Women Veterans Program Manager.

items.name: DAV Women Veterans Programs
items.description: DAV provides free claims help and women-focused outreach; use DAV service officers for gender-specific disability and MST-related claims support.

items.name: National Veterans Legal Services Program (NVLSP)
items.description: Free and low-cost legal representation on VA claims, discharge upgrades, and related Veterans benefits disputes.

items.name: NVLSP Lawyers Serving Warriors
items.description: NVLSP program matching Veterans with pro bono attorneys for complex benefits and discharge-upgrade cases.

items.name: VA Discharge Upgrade Information
items.description: Official VA guidance on how character of discharge affects benefits and where to start a discharge review or upgrade.

items.name: Department of Labor USERRA / VETS
items.description: Federal enforcement and guidance on Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act job protections for service members.

items.name: SWAN Case Management & Legal Referrals
items.description: SWAN maintains vetted pro bono resources and a 24/7 assistance hotline (888-502-8755) for servicewomen and women Veterans facing legal and benefits barriers.

items.name: SBA Office of Veterans Business Development
items.description: U.S. Small Business Administration hub for Veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs—lending, contracting, and counseling resources.

items.name: Veterans Business Outreach Centers (VBOC)
items.description: SBA-funded centers providing free business counseling, training, and mentorship tailored to Veterans and military spouses.

items.name: Boots to Business
items.description: Free SBA entrepreneurship course delivered as part of DoD TAP for transitioning service members, Veterans, and spouses.

items.name: SCORE Mentoring
items.description: Nationwide network of volunteer mentors offering free business mentoring; many chapters have Veteran-focused mentors and workshops.

items.name: Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans (EBV) — IVMF
items.description: Syracuse University IVMF entrepreneurship programs for post-9/11 Veterans, including intensive startup training and founder support.

items.name: VA Office of Small & Disadvantaged Business Utilization (OSDBU)
items.description: VA office that helps Veteran-owned and service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses pursue VA contracting opportunities.

items.name: VA Vendor Information Pages / VOSB Verification
items.description: Entry point for Veteran-owned and service-disabled Veteran-owned small business verification and VA contracting support.

items.name: Team Rubicon
items.description: Disaster-response nonprofit that deploys Veterans and first responders for domestic and international relief missions.

items.name: The Mission Continues
items.description: Connects Veterans to community service missions and leadership opportunities that rebuild purpose after military service.

items.name: Move United
items.description: National adaptive sports organization (merger of Disabled Sports USA and Adaptive Sports USA) with programs for wounded Warriors.

items.name: Travis Manion Foundation
items.description: Character and service programs for Veterans, families of the fallen, and youth—community events and mentorship nationwide.

items.name: Challenge America
items.description: Arts-based programs and peer community for Veterans, including creative workshops and support networks.

items.name: Team Red, White & Blue
items.description: Fitness-centered community that helps Veterans build social connection through local workouts, races, and service events.

items.name: United Service Organizations (USO)
items.description: Global network of centers and programs supporting service members and families from enlistment through deployment and transition home.

items.name: VFW Unmet Needs
items.description: VFW grants (typically up to $2,500) for eligible military families facing financial hardship for basic living expenses.

items.name: American Legion Temporary Financial Assistance
items.description: One-time grants through local Legion posts to help minor children of eligible Veterans and service members with essential needs.

items.name: Army Emergency Relief
items.description: Official Army aid society providing interest-free loans and grants to Soldiers and families in financial emergency.

items.name: Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society
items.description: Financial assistance, budgeting help, and emergency aid for Sailors, Marines, and their families.

items.name: Air & Space Forces Aid Society
items.description: Official charity of the Air Force and Space Force offering emergency loans/grants and education assistance for Airmen, Guardians, and families.

items.name: Operation Homefront Critical Financial Assistance
items.description: Emergency financial help for qualifying military and Veteran families covering essentials like rent, utilities, and food.

items.name: VA Pension
items.description: Needs-based monthly payments for wartime Veterans (and some survivors) with limited income who meet age or disability criteria.

items.name: Coast Guard Mutual Assistance
items.description: Official Coast Guard aid society offering emergency financial assistance, education loans/grants, and counseling for Coast Guard members and families.

items.name: DoD Transition Assistance Program
items.description: Mandatory transition curriculum for separating/retiring service members—career readiness, benefits briefs, and counseling.

items.name: DoD SkillBridge Program
items.description: Approved civilian job training and internship opportunities for service members nearing separation, with command approval.

items.name: VA Benefits for Transitioning Service Members
items.description: VA overview of time-sensitive benefits to consider before and after separation, including health care enrollment and claims.

items.name: Hire Heroes USA — Transition Support
items.description: Personalized career coaching specifically for service members and spouses navigating the military-to-civilian job search.

items.name: Hiring Our Heroes Fellowships
items.description: SkillBridge-approved 12-week corporate and skills-based fellowships connecting transitioning members with hiring employers.

items.name: Military OneSource — Transition
items.description: DoD counseling and resources covering separation planning, spouse employment, financial readiness, and post-service benefits.

items.name: USO Transition Programs
items.description: USO workshops and one-on-one transition support covering education, employment, financial readiness, and mentorship.
